Chapter 9: Sustaining Change—The Practice of Staying Out of the Box.
You know, having a big breakthrough—seeing where you’ve been stuck, stepping out of your own box, maybe even mending a tough relationship—it’s powerful. But here’s the real challenge: how do you keep that change alive? Old habits don’t just disappear. Everyday pressures can easily nudge us right back into the box before we even realize it.
So, what if getting out of the box isn’t a one-time event? What if it’s more like a practice—something you choose, over and over, no matter how many times you drift back? Every day, you’ll find fresh chances to spot those old patterns sneaking in. When you catch yourself, just pause and give yourself the space to choose a different response.
Some folks make this easier by creating little reminders—a sticky note on the monitor, a question to ask before jumping into a meeting, or even a few quiet moments to check in before a tough conversation. Others lean on trusted friends or coworkers, asking them to speak up if they notice any defensiveness, or if you start closing off.
Let me give you an example. There was this team that really wanted to stay out of the box, so they tried something new. Before every meeting, they’d ask, “Is there anything I need to own before we start?” It felt awkward at first—who likes starting with that?—but after a while, it changed everything. People got honest, mistakes were admitted quickly, and any tension was cleared before it could get out of hand.
Here’s something to remember: give yourself some grace. Nobody stays out of the box all the time. You’ll have setbacks, get frustrated, or slip back into old stories now and then. What matters most is noticing, taking responsibility, and giving it another try.
And don’t forget why this practice matters. When you’re out of the box, your relationships feel closer, your work has more purpose, and life just feels lighter. The effort isn’t just for you—it ripples out to everyone around you.
With time, this practice gets easier. The grip of the box loosens, and new habits start to grow. The journey never really ends, but each step brings more freedom, connection, and possibility.
